card.name: Verbs and pronouns after a subject noun
card.fires_on: A single word right after a subject in general news or web prose, such as a verb (reached, believe, will), a pronoun (we, own) or a linking word (if, with, than, of). The word comes just before the rest of a clause.

modes.label: Verb after subject
modes.description: A verb or auxiliary right after a subject like jury, team or we.
modes.example: the group discusses what occurred at the trial and why the jury<< reached>> its verdict.

modes.label: Pronoun or possessive
modes.description: A pronoun or 'own' that points back to a group mentioned earlier.
modes.example: Nepal needs to learn from its<< own>> successes in

modes.label: Linking word mid-clause
modes.description: A small word such as if, with, of or than that continues a clause.
modes.example: They might well have been executed<< if>> national and international groups had not pressured

card.plain: It marks a small word in the middle of an ordinary sentence, right after the subject, where the clause is about to continue.
